text:
alex: quick sync — noticed 3 onboarding failures in the last week that weren't caught by the current smoke harness. can we map out failure modes and a minimal set of checks to catch them early?

maria: yes. what were the failures? short list please.

alex: 1) tokenizer mismatch -> model tokenizes differently than our golden inputs 2) kv-cache blowups on long prompts (OOM/latency spike) 3) perf nondeterminism across quantized builds (30% tail latency variance)

jon: for tokenizer mismatch we should add a small tokenization parity check: run 100 golden sentences through model tokenizer + reference tokenizer and fail if token sequences differ. quick to run.

tara: +1. also add a certificate in model metadata for tokenizer_version so we can auto-bypass models that intentionally change tokenization. that helps rollouts.

alex: proposal: two-layer onboarding: 1) lightweight smoke (sec/min) to catch tokenization & basic infer correctness + kv sanity, 2) async bench (longer) for perf stability and tail latency sampling. if smoke fails, block immediate admission. if bench flags nondet, mark model as "needs-stable-quant" and route to canary.

maria: does smoke include a tiny golden replay of user traces? we could keep ~50 short/long traces (mix) and check outputs for major divergence or logits crash.

jon: sample smoke job config:```yaml
smoke:
  inputs: golden_50.json
  checks:
    - token_parity
    - infer_success
    - kv_cache_limit: 1GB
    - max_tail_latency_ms: 200
```

tara: what about models that intentionally have slightly different output distributions? we need fuzzy matching thresholds to avoid false positives. store per-model baseline diffs as metadata.

alex: agree — store baseline metrics (emd/levenshtein/token-diff rates) in registry after first full bench. smoke compares against baseline with permissive thresholds. async bench computes stricter regressions.

benchbot: CI: smoke run for model "open-xyz-v1" completed: token_parity=FAIL, kv_cache=OK, infer_success=OK -> created ticket #ML-422.

maria: benchbot output is helpful. can we auto-attach a triage checklist to tickets? e.g., "is tokenizer mapping intentional?" "does model include new special tokens?"

jon: +1. triage checklist will reduce chatter. suggest fields: tokenizer_version, quantization_profile, expected_max_kv_bytes, golden_input_hashes.

alex: next steps: 1) small RFC doc with failure-mode map + proposed smoke job the week of Mon, 2) add token_parity & baseline metadata to registry API, 3) benchbot attach checklist on FAIL. i'll draft RFC and ping owners.

tara: sounds good. tagging @maria for registry API changes.

maria: i'll own registry fields. jon I'll pair on smoke harness. thanks.

alex: thanks all — will drop RFC link here when done :thumbsup:
